question: A 72-year-old male visits his gastroenterologist for a check-up one year following resection of a 2-cm malignant lesion in his sigmoid colon. Serum levels of which of the following can be used in this patient to test for cancer recurrence?
analysis: Carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) is a tumor marker commonly used to monitor for recurrence of colorectal cancer after treatment. It is not used for diagnosis but can be helpful in follow-up care to detect potential recurrence. Alpha-fetoprotein is associated with liver cancer and germ cell tumors, CA-125 is used for ovarian cancer, gamma glutamyl transferase is a liver enzyme, and CA-19-9 is associated with pancreatic cancer.
